tourist: If Diddy already knows what he does that's foolish and stupid, why can't he become wise? Act wisely. For, oh, Diddy has perceived his follies countless times. Is heartily ashamed of them, strenuously repudiates them. It's only that he doesn't understand. Not really. A hopeless, bumbling tourist in the somber labyrinth of his own consciousness.

I stared at this earnest young black man for a moment. Suddenly my hair became very political. Waves of horror washed over me. How many forms of religious persecution are we now going to visit upon one another as black people in the name of our public safety? And suppose I was a Rastafarian? What then? Why did that automatically mean I could not vacation in Virgin Gorda? Did it make my tourist dollars unusable?
touch:
I like for you to be still: it is as though you were absent,
and you hear me from far away and my voice does not touch you.
Veinte Poemas de Amor y una Canción Desesperada (Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair) (1924)
I usually dislike my books, sometimes, don't want to touch them. But the Next One will be a bit better. I am always excited and forget all failures and all else.
Between me and life is a faint glass. No matter how sharply I see and understand life, I cannot touch it.
And there are things that are hard to talk about—you'll rub off their marvelous pollen at the touch of a word.
Letter to then-girlfriend Véra (26 July 1923); in Letters to Véra (2014), p 3.
Even error was a discovery. Erring would make her find the other face of objects and touch their dusty sides.

To be in love
Is to touch with a lighter hand.
In yourself you stretch, you are well.
tough: Wars are Spinach. Life in general is the tough part. In war all you have to do is not worry and know how to read a map and co-ordinates.
touched: Having touched Christ's feet is not an excuse for punctuation mistakes.
A Factless Autobiography, Richard Zenith Edition, Lisbon, 2006, p 229
touches: I sleep and I unsleep. On the other side of me, beyond where I lie down, the silence of the house touches infinity. I hear time falling, drop by drop, and no falling drop is heard falling.

Nothing touches a work of art so little as words of criticism : they always result in more or less fortunate misunderstandings. Things aren't all so tangible and sayable as people would usually have us believe; most experiences are unsayable, they happen in a space that no word has ever entered, and more unsayable than all other things are works of art, those mysterious existences, whose life endures beside our own small, transitory life.
